html:
The great Doric temple of Zeus at Olympia, the sanctuary of the Olympic Games, built around 470 to 456 BCE. Its architect was Libon of Elis. It was the largest temple in the Peloponnese.

Its sculptures are among the best of the early Classical style:

  • the east pediment showed the chariot race of Pelops, the myth of the founding of the games
  • the west pediment showed the fight of the Lapiths and Centaurs, with Apollo calm in the middle
  • the metopes showed the twelve labours of Heracles

Around 435 BCE Phidias made for it a huge seated statue of Zeus in gold and ivory, counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Visitors said the god seemed so large that if he stood up he would break through the roof.

The temple was thrown down by earthquakes in the 6th century CE. Its huge column drums still lie where they fell. The temple set a standard that the Parthenon soon followed.
sum: The great Doric temple of Zeus at Olympia, the sanctuary of the Olympic Games, built around 470 to 456 BCE. Its architect was Libon of Elis. It was the largest temple in the Peloponnese.
